title: Star Trek: Picard Almost Starred Uhura Instead
summary:
Before Star Trek: Picard became the final voyage of Captain Jean-Luc Picard, it almost told a very different story. The show's first idea starred someone else entirely: Nyota Uhura.

According to an interview with TrekCore, Picard co-creators Alex Kurtzman and Kristen Beyer began with a plan to bring back Nichelle Nichols, who played Uhura, the communications officer of the original Enterprise. It would have been her first return to the role since 1991.

The very first idea was a meeting between Uhura and a very young Picard. Kurtzman said the young Picard would have been called to a hospital, where Uhura had a mission for him — and it was related to the Borg, the villains who later starred in Picard.

It is a fascinating what-if. Uhura was groundbreaking, yet badly underused in the original series — her scenes were sometimes rewritten to shrink her role. Her portrayal featured television's first interracial kiss and was praised by Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. Yet Uhura is the only original bridge crew member who never returned after Star Trek VI: The Undiscovered Country. Nichols turned down a small cameo on Star Trek: Voyager, and she passed away in 2022.

The idea raises fun questions. The Next Generation takes place nearly 100 years after the original series, so how could they meet? Star Trek has bent time before: Scotty returned in 'Relics,' Spock lived well into his second century, and a 137-year-old Dr. McCoy appeared in the pilot of The Next Generation.

Then there is the Borg problem. They were completely unknown when the Enterprise first met them in the second season of The Next Generation. Could Uhura have known about them years earlier? The Borg are no strangers to time travel — but a warning could have saved the Federation a lot of trouble.
why_it_matters: The what-if shows how much one character can matter: Uhura broke ground on television but was given too little to do, and the abandoned idea hints at the bigger story she might have had.

background_read: Star Trek is a long-running science-fiction series about the crew of a starship exploring space, and the original series starred Captain Kirk and his crew, including Uhura, the communications officer.
Star Trek: The Next Generation is set about a century later and follows a new crew led by Captain Jean-Luc Picard, while Star Trek: Picard continues Picard's story years after that.
The Borg are a powerful group of villains in Star Trek who turn other beings into part of their collective, and they were a major threat in both The Next Generation and Picard.

Uhura, played by Nichelle Nichols, was one of the first Black women in a major role on American television, which is why her character is remembered as groundbreaking even though her part was often small.
